corpus_fragility.meaning: Links are point-pair witnesses; edges are collection-pair equality constraints. All baseline links are exported because the baseline is consistent and has no cuts.

finding.classification: parameter-sensitive equality matching candidate; physical error unconfirmed
finding.conclusion: The single borderline witness is not the sole support. Radial tightening alone and a support minimum of 5 preserve the edge. Joint tightening to 0.25D and 3 degrees removes it in all three z settings. All baseline witnesses compare different angles. This is a candidate angular-alias matching weakness in legacy 0.2.1, not proof that the equality is physically false. Stability alone cannot locate the fault elsewhere in the order cycle.

crowding_interpretation.legacy_veto: No target neighbourhood was vetoed in the baseline or the 27-point sweep.
crowding_interpretation.observability: There are zero adjacent-label crowding tests in these target neighbourhoods. All three target traces are single-z and constant-label; the legacy veto is uninformative here, not a clearance certificate.
crowding_interpretation.descriptive_geometry: At common angles, linear interpolation puts same:150 and same:151 less than 0.7D apart at 19 of 65 evaluation knots (minimum 9.591 voxels). This suggests possible local close spacing but does not establish that they are adjacent physical wraps. same:149 versus same:151 stays at least 32.071 voxels apart in the same-angle interpolation.
crowding_interpretation.limitations: Sampling density and angular interpolation uncertainty are not calibrated; no CT surface, sheet normal or physical adjacency is available. Knot counts are not area fractions.

measurement_notes: All matching runs call the unchanged 0.2.1 build_links; no order module is imported.
The 27-grid varies the radial factor, angular window and z window only. Support thresholds are evaluated separately.
Crowding instrumentation duplicates the legacy cell-veto arithmetic and its global veto count is asserted equal to build_links in every sweep setting.
Point-pair support is not the number of statistically independent observations.
The corpus comparison holds every setting except r_same fixed; links additionally disappear when their remaining collection-pair support drops below two.
